d: Crowded endometrial glands with cytologic atypia, equivalent to atypical hyperplasia. It often shows PTEN loss, frequently coexists with endometrioid carcinoma, and is treated by hysterectomy or high-dose progestin with close follow-up.
The DNA repair system, built from MLH1, MSH2, MSH6 and PMS2, that fixes copying errors. Inherited loss causes Lynch syndrome, with microsatellite instability in the tumors.
An ovarian cyst lined by endometriosis and filled with thick brown blood from repeated cyclic bleeding, which is why it is called a chocolate cyst. It causes pain and infertility.

Endometrial glands and stroma lying within the myometrium. The muscle thickens around them, making a uniformly enlarged, soft, globular uterus with heavy, painful periods, usually in multiparous women in their 40s.
The swirling pattern of interlacing smooth muscle bundles on the cut surface of a leiomyoma. The sharp edge and bland cells separate it from leiomyosarcoma, which is soft, hemorrhagic and necrotic.
Intrauterine adhesions that replace the basalis after curettage or infection. The cavity cannot rebuild a lining, so patients have secondary amenorrhea and infertility with normal hormone levels.
